basis.text: Xamarin.Forms NuGet packages are generally not compatible with .NET unless rebuilt for .NET target frameworks; without a compatible version, a package is rebuilt, taken in a preview or replaced

basis.text: support for the Xamarin SDKs, Xamarin.Forms included, has ended with no further fixes or updates, and the policy points Xamarin.Forms apps to .NET MAUI and Xamarin.Android and Xamarin.iOS apps to .NET for Android and .NET for iOS

findings.own: a package reference of a project or packages.config whose id matches an entry of packageMap with "use": null; the table names such packages only when the configuration does, because whether a library has a .NET version is a fact the tool cannot look up; an error, because the app cannot build on .NET MAUI until the package is replaced or rebuilt

findings.found: the class AndroidShadowEffect is a PlatformEffect, exported by ExportEffect at examples/messy/TidewaterDriver.Android/Effects/AndroidShadowEffect.cs:6: on .NET MAUI the effect is registered with ConfigureEffects, with no ExportEffect or ResolutionGroupName attribute
findings.fix: remove the ExportEffect and ResolutionGroupName attributes, put the platform effects next to their RoutingEffect with conditional compilation, and register the pair with ConfigureEffects in MauiProgram; or move the customization to a handler

basis.text: Xamarin.Forms effects can be reused once the ExportEffect and ResolutionGroupName attributes are removed, the platform effects sit with the routing effect, and the effect is registered with ConfigureEffects
basis.source: Reuse effects in .NET MAUI (Microsoft Learn)

findings.own: a C# class that derives from PlatformEffect, and an ExportEffect assembly attribute that names an effect no scanned class declares; the RoutingEffect classes are counted in the summary

findings.found: the class RoundedEntryRenderer derives from EntryRenderer, a Xamarin.Forms renderer, registered for RoundedEntry by ExportRenderer at examples/messy/TidewaterDriver.Android/Renderers/RoundedEntryRenderer.cs:8: renderers become handlers on .NET MAUI
findings.fix: move the customization to a .NET MAUI handler: a PropertyMapper entry, or a handler of its own registered with ConfigureMauiHandlers; a renderer that derives from VisualElementRenderer, ListViewRenderer, FrameRenderer or TableViewRenderer can be kept for a while through the shims, registered with AddHandler, with its ExportRenderer attribute removed

basis.text: .NET MAUI replaces custom renderers with handlers, which map each property to its own method, create no parent view and are registered in MauiProgram rather than found by assembly scanning
basis.source: Migrate a custom renderer to a .NET MAUI handler (Microsoft Learn)

basis.text: renderers that derive from a few base classes, such as VisualElementRenderer, ListViewRenderer or FrameRenderer, can be reused through shims once the ExportRenderer attributes are removed and the renderers are registered with AddHandler

findings.fix: target .NET instead: net8.0-android for Android, net8.0-ios for iOS, net8.0-maccatalyst for the Mac and net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0 for Windows (or the same names for the .NET version you move to), with the minimum OS version in SupportedOSPlatformVersion

basis.text: a .NET for Android project is SDK-style with a target such as net8.0-android, and the minimum Android version moves from the uses-sdk element of AndroidManifest.xml to SupportedOSPlatformVersion

basis.text: support for the Xamarin SDKs, Xamarin.Forms included, has ended with no further fixes or updates, and the policy points Xamarin.Forms apps to .NET MAUI and Xamarin.Android and Xamarin.iOS apps to .NET for Android and .NET for iOS
